question: Can a diffusion model replace isotropic white noise with dataset-matched scale-invariant Gaussian noise so that every spatial frequency has comparable signal-to-noise ratio throughout diffusion, and would that improve sampling speed, detail, and controllability?

key_findings.claim: On the cleaned grayscale STL10 subset studied, the Fourier transform approximately diagonalizes the empirical pixel covariance and its diagonal follows a radial inverse power law with fitted scaling parameter near 1.5.
key_findings.evidence: The real-space covariance shows nearby-pixel correlation. After masking the prominent horizontal/vertical Fourier cross, off-diagonal Fourier covariances are visually close to zero and a log-log fit gives Gamma_diag(k) approximately A squared divided by |k| to the power 2 Delta, with Delta about 1.5. The paper names a Gaussian with this fitted spectrum 'Cloud Noise.'

key_findings.claim: The proposed cloud-noise sampler colors white noise by a power-law Fourier filter, but practical aperiodic images require an explicit boundary workaround.
key_findings.evidence: The construction Fourier-transforms white noise, divides modes by |k|^Delta, and inverts. Direct use imposes toroidal periodicity, so the implementation generates a field with roughly triple linear extent, crops its center, and renormalizes variance; this reduces but does not analytically eliminate boundary effects.

key_findings.claim: Scale-invariant Gaussian noise with a fixed exponent is closed under the weighted sums used by standard DDPM forward marginals.
key_findings.evidence: The paper introduces a real-valued rearrangement of the FFT's independent degrees of freedom and models transformed noise with diagonal covariance A squared |k|^{-2 Delta} I. Adding independent scaled draws changes only the overall covariance amplitude by alpha squared plus beta squared, preserving Delta, so the usual jump formula x_t = sqrt(alpha_bar_t)x_0 + sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)epsilon remains available.

key_findings.claim: Under the paper's covariance-matching approximation, cloud diffusion preserves a frequency-independent signal-to-noise ratio, unlike white-noise diffusion's low-to-high-frequency reverse ordering.
key_findings.evidence: If both data and terminal noise share the same power-law covariance shape, every intermediate convex Gaussian mixture retains it; the signal and noise spectra differ by only global time coefficients. With white noise, high-frequency data energy is smaller and therefore falls below noise earlier, so reverse sampling reveals low frequencies before high ones.

key_findings.claim: The only quantitative proximity check shows cloud noise closer than white noise under a chosen Mahalanobis construction, not a shorter learned diffusion trajectory.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines expected Mahalanobis distances between sampled distributions relative to a covariance reference and reports a plotted ordering in which Cloud Noise is closer to the image set than white noise. It does not calculate Wasserstein, path length, likelihood, or the number of reverse solver steps for a trained cloud model.

key_findings.claim: Claims of better high-frequency detail and guidance are mechanism hypotheses, not results of a trained-model comparison in this paper.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 4.2-4.3 argue that simultaneous frequency refinement should reduce late-step overconstraint and let high-frequency prompts influence early structure, illustrated with generic generated images and a hypothetical Where's Waldo task. The abstract explicitly defers implementation and comparison to a follow-up; no cloud diffusion network is trained, sampled, or evaluated here.

key_findings.claim: The method matches only pooled second-order spectral statistics, so it cannot by itself make the Gaussian terminal distribution close to the multimodal semantic image distribution in a strong generative sense.
key_findings.evidence: Cloud Noise is a zero-mean Gaussian fully specified by a radial covariance fit after masking anisotropic cross structure. Natural-image phase, orientation, higher-order dependencies, color-channel coupling, objects, and semantics remain absent. Equal covariance shape is therefore a useful preconditioner hypothesis rather than a distributional equivalence.

anchors.section: Cloud Diffusion overview and closeness claim

method.core_idea: Use the empirical power spectrum of natural images as a preconditioning covariance for the diffusion terminal Gaussian, so forward noising preserves the dataset's low-order spectral shape rather than flattening it with white noise.
method.mechanism: The paper estimates a radial Fourier covariance exponent from a cleaned grayscale STL10 subset, creates colored Gaussian fields by power-law Fourier filtering and cropping, proves closure of the resulting covariance family under DDPM weighted sums, and compares time-dependent frequency SNR plus a Mahalanobis proximity measure to white noise.
assumptions: A single radial second-order power law adequately summarizes the relevant natural-image spectrum.
Masked Fourier modes and crop-based boundary correction do not materially distort the fitted covariance.
Frequency covariance is close enough to diagonal that independent Fourier coefficients are an effective model.
Matching terminal and data covariance shapes makes reverse dynamics easier for a learned denoiser.
Uniform frequency SNR is preferable to coarse-to-fine generation for quality and conditioning.

techniques.role: Estimates the dataset-specific exponent Delta from the Fourier covariance diagonal.
Generates Gaussian fields with covariance proportional to |k|^{-2 Delta}.
Rearranges conjugate FFT degrees of freedom into a real vector with diagonal covariance.
Shows DDPM weighted sums preserve the colored-noise exponent.
Contrasts white-noise spectral autoregression with simultaneous frequency refinement.
Provides the paper's quantitative but reference-dependent closeness comparison.

evaluations.metric: Fourier covariance off-diagonal structure and log-log radial slope after masking the central cross
evaluations.result: Approximately diagonal covariance with fitted Delta near 1.5

evaluations.setting: Dataset samples, matched cloud-noise samples, and matched white-noise samples
evaluations.metric: Expected Mahalanobis distance under selected reference covariances
evaluations.result: Figure 19 places cloud noise closer to the image set than white noise under the reported construction

evaluations.setting: Analytical DDPM covariance interpolation in Fourier coordinates
evaluations.metric: Signal-to-noise ratio as a function of frequency and diffusion time
evaluations.result: Dataset-matched colored noise gives frequency-independent SNR in the covariance model; white noise suppresses high-frequency SNR first

limitations: This Part 1 paper does not train or evaluate a Cloud Diffusion model.
Speed, detail, and controllability claims are predictions without NFE, FID, likelihood, human-preference, or prompt-adherence results.
The fit uses a cleaned grayscale STL10 subset and a manually masked spectral cross, so cross-dataset and color generality are unknown.
A radial Gaussian covariance discards phase, anisotropy, higher-order statistics, and semantic multimodality.
The crop-based aperiodic-noise workaround changes the intended spectrum and is justified empirically rather than with an exact covariance calculation.
Uniform frequency corruption may remove a useful coarse-to-fine inductive bias on ordinary natural-image tasks.
failure_modes: An incorrectly fitted spectral exponent can overweight low frequencies or inject excessive high-frequency energy.
FFT boundary periodicity can create seam correlations unless the enlarged-field crop is sufficiently conservative.
Near-zero frequency requires explicit numerical treatment because the power-law filter is singular.
A dataset with classes or channels having different spectra may be poorly served by one pooled covariance.
Colored noise may make terminal sampling or score weighting ill-conditioned even when the forward marginal is algebraically valid.
reusable_insights: Treat the terminal Gaussian covariance as a learnable preconditioner and evaluate it jointly with the noise schedule.
Plot per-frequency SNR and residual error across time to expose hidden spectral ordering in a diffusion system.
Compare a covariance-matched prior against whitened-data training, non-isotropic diffusion, and deterministic spectral degradations under equal compute.
Dataset-level power spectra are cheap diagnostics but should be supplemented by class-, channel-, and orientation-conditioned spectra.
open_questions: Does learned colored-noise diffusion reduce NFE at matched FID and recall on diverse natural-image datasets?
Should the spectral covariance be fixed, learned end-to-end, conditioned on class/text, or allowed to vary over time?
How does uniform frequency SNR interact with latent autoencoders whose representation already reshapes the spectrum?
Can a full-covariance or wavelet prior capture orientation and locality without losing efficient sampling?
Which prospective metrics would falsify the proposed shorter-path mechanism rather than merely show an empirical win?

competitive_landscape.title: A Fourier Space Perspective on Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Independently derives the unequal-frequency corruption problem and actually trains an equal-rate Fourier forward process, reporting gains on high-frequency tasks and parity on standard benchmarks; Cloud Diffusion Part 1 supplies a natural-image power-law motivation but defers model evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Flicker-DDPM: Accelerating Denoising Diffusion via 1/f Colored Noise Injection
competitive_landscape.difference: Implements a tunable power-law spatial correlation kernel and reports CIFAR-10 quality with 3.33 times fewer sampling steps, providing a later empirical test of the central colored-noise acceleration hypothesis.

competitive_landscape.title: Score-based Denoising Diffusion with Non-Isotropic Gaussian Noise Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Derives score-based diffusion for general non-isotropic Gaussian covariance and supplies CIFAR-10 samples; Cloud Diffusion specializes covariance to a dataset power law and emphasizes equal spectral SNR.

competitive_landscape.title: Blurring Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Recasts heat dissipation as non-isotropic Gaussian diffusion and combines blur with standard noise; its forward process deliberately removes high frequencies, whereas cloud noise aims to equalize their SNR trajectory.

competitive_landscape.title: Cold Diffusion: Inverting Arbitrary Image Transforms Without Noise
competitive_landscape.difference: Shows generative iterative restoration can invert blur, masking, and other deterministic degradations, challenging the need for Gaussian noise entirely; Cloud Diffusion stays within Gaussian DDPM algebra and changes its covariance.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Dataset-matched scale-invariant Gaussian noise preserves equal signal-to-noise ratio across frequencies and should yield a shorter, more holistic reverse process with faster inference, better detail, and stronger high-frequency control.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper fits a power-law covariance, proves closure under DDPM sums, derives the spectral-SNR contrast, and reports a Mahalanobis proximity ordering.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The conceptual preconditioner is coherent, but the closest concurrent paper already implements an equal-rate Fourier process, and later Flicker-DDPM tests colored-noise acceleration. This paper's independent value is its accessible natural-image scaling derivation and specific cloud-noise construction, not demonstrated generative superiority.

reviewer_notes: Read all 39 pages, including the covariance analysis, boundary treatment, real-FFT construction, closure derivation, SNR arguments, motivation sections, acknowledgments, and references. Current primary competitors and revision numbers were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
